items.description: Math.floor((score - 10) / 2) — the D&D ability modifier formula — appears in 6 files: CharacterInfoSection.tsx:33, DnDSkills.tsx:11, SavingThrowsDisplay.tsx:17, DnDSavingThrows.tsx:11, diceCalculations.ts:27, Phase1Demo.tsx:172. This is a rendering rule violation: the web is calculating game mechanics. The API should provide computed modifier values.

applyMonsterMovement at LobbyView.tsx:89 is a module-level function that transforms Room entity positions. It is not extracted in either PR #377 or PR #378 (only entityStateToPlacement, roomFromEncounterState, doorsFromEncounterState, monstersFromEncounterState were extracted). It belongs in utils/monsterTurnUtils.ts or similar.

src/concepts/class-selection/data.ts contains hardcoded class descriptions, ability score guidance, and level progression tables. If this concept is promoted, the data layer must be replaced with API calls — hardcoded game data in the web layer violates the rendering rules.

Both ActionPanel.tsx and ActionPanelV2.tsx exist and are exported from combat-v2/panels/index.ts. No documentation explains which supersedes the other or which LobbyView actually uses. Needs clarification and deprecation of one.

items.summary: OpenDoor reveal stores room-B walls and entities without translating from room-local to dungeon-absolute, so revealed rooms overlap room A geometrically

MovementCompletedEvent for players carries entityId+path but omits updatedEntity, so handleMovementCompleted in LobbyView never advanced the character position in encounterState. Fix mirrors applyMonsterMovement: fall back on path[path.length-1] via new mergeEntityPosition helper. Stream dispatch was already correct (useEncounterStream.ts:127). Branch fix/wave2-player-move-render, commit 0d82258. Awaiting Kirk playtest verification.

Three layered web-side gates blocked cross-room play: (1) BattleMapPanel.tsx:75-81 filtered entities by entity.roomId === currentRoomId so the player vanished when a new room was revealed; (2) HexGrid.tsx isBlocked treated any non-floor-tile as impassable, but doors sit on the boundary and are in NEITHER room's bbox so A* refused to path through open doors — root of 'client never lets me cross'; (3) handleRoomRevealed had no console.log so the dispatcher's correct delivery was invisible during playtest. Fixed by removing the entity filter, adding openDoorWalkableKeys to extend isBlocked, and adding a structured log. Branch fix/wave2-player-move-render commit 26238ee. All conceptually the same shape — web treating currentRoomId as singular focus instead of accepting all revealed rooms as first-class. Per feedback_no_logic_in_web.

AdvancedCharacterShader's vertexShader missed the instanceMatrix multiply, so every InstancedMesh tile rendered at the geometry's local origin. ShadedHexFloor wraps every revealed-room floor tile in one InstancedMesh keyed off this shader; without `instanceMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0)` all 18*16 = 288 floor tiles stacked at world (0,0,0) and Kirk only ever saw a single hex at the corner — initially mis-described as 'movement range outline only'. Three.js auto-defines USE_INSTANCING and provides the instanceMatrix attribute, but it does NOT auto-rewrite a custom ShaderMaterial's vertexShader source — that's on the author. Fix wraps position+normal transform in `#ifdef USE_INSTANCING` and threads instanceColor through `vInstanceColor` for per-tile shading variation + hover/door highlights. Non-instanced character/hair/non-instanced wall paths preserved via #else branch. Pure-function tile-accumulation tests in useDungeonMap.test.ts had been green throughout — bug was below them (render output collapsed to origin). Same commit also fixes roomFromEncounterState only building the current room's RoomLayout (`data.currentRoomId` is still room A on RoomRevealed since opening a door doesn't move the player); added roomsFromEncounterState that iterates every entry in `data.rooms` with current room ordered last. Branch fix/wave2-player-move-render commit 573fa40. Lessons: a green pure-function test layer doesn't prove the render path; custom ShaderMaterial + InstancedMesh = remember to use instanceMatrix; a 'movement range outline' that shrinks correctly proves floor data IS populated and pushes the bug to the render-side.

TurnState.movementUsed and TurnState.movementMax are deprecated proto fields; the canonical source is TurnState.actionEconomy.movementRemaining. Web call sites used `(movementMax || 30) - (movementUsed || 0)` everywhere, and the api converter at converters.go:436 fills movementUsed from `30 - state.MovementRemaining` on a code path that desyncs from actionEconomy across OpenDoor (Wave 2). When the deprecated path reported 0 ft remaining while actionEconomy still said 30, the web's range indicator (useMovementRange.getReachableHexes returned empty Set), pathing into revealed rooms (useHexInteraction gated isWithinRange on movementRemaining), and any non-adjacent attack (same gate) all silently broke. Adjacent attacks worked because pathCost=0. Single root cause for the three Wave 2 post-shader-fix symptoms. Fix: new utils/movementUtils.ts as the only place that reads movement-remaining; resolution order is canonical actionEconomy → deprecated subtraction → 0. BattleMapPanel and LobbyView's validateAndExecuteMove now route through it. Diagnostic logs added in handleMovementCompleted (canonical vs deprecated values) and HexGrid (reachable-tiles size + sample on player turn). Five other call sites (CombatOverlay, CombatActionPanel, DebugPanel, usePlayerTurn, ActionEconomyIndicators) still read deprecated; display-only and out of scope for this commit. Branch fix/wave2-player-move-render commit 86694de. Lesson: `@deprecated` proto fields are toxic when other fields can carry the same data — pick canonical-first reads and have ONE helper, not inline subtractions everywhere.
